sccomp_simulate

Source: R/simulate_data.R
sccomp_simulate.Rd

Simulate counts from a fitted sccomp model, optionally replacing the abundance coefficients and the mean-variability association with user-chosen values. Variability is not taken from the posterior: for every variability term it is derived from the abundance coefficient it is associated with, alpha = beta * slope + intercept, plus the fitted residual scatter around that trend (see variability_scatter), so changing the abundance coefficients changes the simulated variability as the model expects. Random effects and the remaining parameters come from the posterior draws.

Usage

sccomp_simulate(
  fit,
  formula_composition,
  formula_variability = NULL,
  new_data = NULL,
  coefficients = NULL,
  mean_dispersion_slope = NULL,
  mean_dispersion_intercept = NULL,
  sample = NULL,
  cell_group = NULL,
  variability_multiplier = 1,
  number_of_draws = 1,
  mcmc_seed = sample_seed(),
  cores = detectCores(),
  sig_figs = 9,
  cache_stan_model = sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir,
  variability_scatter = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

The result of sccomp_estimate execution. This is used for sampling from real-data properties.

formula_composition

A formula. The formula describing the model for differential abundance, for example ~treatment. It can be a sub-formula of the fitted one.

formula_variability

A formula. The formula describing the model for differential variability, for example ~treatment. If NULL, the fitted variability formula is used.

new_data

A tibble including sample-specific columns (sample identifier and factor columns from formula). If coefficients are provided separately, cell_group column is optional. Otherwise, should include cell_group column. If NULL, the data used for the fit is used.

coefficients

A data frame/tibble with cell-type specific coefficients. Must contain a column matching the cell_group column name with every fitted cell group, and columns matching the design matrix column names (e.g., "(Intercept)", "typecancer"). Design columns that are absent are set to zero. For each design column, the coefficients must sum to zero across cell groups. If NULL, the posterior coefficients are used.

mean_dispersion_slope

Optional slope of the mean-variability association. Either a single number, applied to every variability term, or a vector named by variability design column (e.g. c("(Intercept)" = -0.7)), in which case unnamed terms keep their posterior slope. If NULL, the posterior slopes are used, or 0 for a model fitted with exclude_mean_variability_association = TRUE.

mean_dispersion_intercept

Optional intercept of the mean-variability association, in the same forms as mean_dispersion_slope. If NULL, the posterior intercepts are used, except for terms whose slope is overridden, which take their posterior-mean intercept so that only the slope changes.

sample

A column name as a character string for the sample identifier. If NULL, the one used for the fit.

cell_group

A column name as a character string for the cell-group identifier. If NULL, the one used for the fit.

variability_multiplier

A real scalar. This can be used for artificially increasing the variability of the simulation for benchmarking purposes.

number_of_draws

An integer. How may copies of the data you want to draw from the model joint posterior distribution.

mcmc_seed

An integer. Used for Markov-chain Monte Carlo reproducibility. By default a random number is sampled from 1 to 999999. This itself can be controlled by set.seed()

cores

Integer, the number of cores to be used for parallel calculations.

sig_figs

Number of significant figures to use for Stan model output. Default is 9.

cache_stan_model

A character string specifying the cache directory for compiled Stan models. The sccomp version will be automatically appended to ensure version isolation. Default is sccomp_stan_models_cache_dir which points to ~/.sccomp_models.

variability_scatter

Logical. If TRUE (default), each cell group's variability is drawn around the mean-variability trend with the fitted residual standard deviation (prec_sd), as fitted cell groups scatter around it. If FALSE, every cell group sits exactly on the trend.

Value

The rows of new_data (expanded to every cell group if new_data has no cell_group column), with the following columns added:

  • generated_proportions - A numeric column representing the generated proportions from the simulation.

  • generated_counts - An integer column representing the generated cell counts from the simulation.

  • replicate - An integer column representing the replicate number for each draw from the posterior distribution.

References

S. Mangiola, A.J. Roth-Schulze, M. Trussart, E. Zozaya-Valdés, M. Ma, Z. Gao, A.F. Rubin, T.P. Speed, H. Shim, & A.T. Papenfuss, sccomp: Robust differential composition and variability analysis for single-cell data, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 120 (33) e2203828120, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2203828120 (2023).
